newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares steady, EA-Generali off 8.24 pct.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares steady, EA-Generali off 8.24 pct.

text.p: Austrian shares ended flat on Thursday as demand for shares in the nation's two biggest banks helped offset heavy selling in EA-Generali, triggered by the insurer's fading hopes for a stake in Creditanstalt.
The ATX index of 21 blue chip shares closed 0.02 points up at 1,121.90 after briefly dipping below support at 1,120. Nine issues were up, nine down and three unchanged.
Creditanstalt ordinaries were among the leading gainers and most actively traded shares after Bank Austria announced it would bid for the state's stake, reportedly offering 804 schillings a share.
Creditanstalt ordinary shares finished 1.7 percent up at 732 schillings on turnover of 65,080 lots.
Bank Austria shares, back after a one-day suspension, finished 1.2 percent up at 417 schillings.

In contrast, shares in EA-Generali tumbled 8.24 percent to 3,120 schillings as investors sensed the insurer's hopes of buying into Creditanstalt were fading. An EA-Generali-led bid reportedly falls a long way short of the Bank Austria offer.
"EA-Generali is under pressure because of the whole Creditanstalt business," said a trader.
"Firstly, it looks as though they may not be successful in their bid and secondly, there is concern that they may lose out on the business they have through Creditanstalt."
The two firms togther operate insurance unit CA-Generali.
Austria's sole motorcycle manufacturer KTM, which made its bourse debut on Thursday, topped turnover and finished at 605 schillings, up from an issue price of 590.
The Vienna bourse index was down 1.18 points at 423.71. December ATX futures stood 2.0 points up at 1,117.0. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
